description: Graded capability record for trusted host-control admission, per exact host version, against the capability ladder: Tier 0 read-only inspection only; Tier 1 mutation floor (deny-until-attested grant enforcement, worktree-materialized digest-receipted projection, binding attestation, a qualified host-owned opaque pre-registration operator-confirmation producer, fence-revocation cancellation, fresh-worktree-only resume); the floor's grant enforcement rests on host workspace scoping, and that control has a stated boundary: the OS sandbox grants the system temporary directory as a writable root independently of the workspace, so a delivery workspace materialized under it is scoped by nothing the host contributes. Such a workspace is accepted rather than refused, because it is this system's normal shape, and it is the binding's own composed ambient-temp denial that scopes it. That denial is emitted under both the written and the resolved spelling of every root, since the OS boundary matches where a path resolves and the temporary directory is a symlink on the graded platform. Tier 2 trusted graceful lifecycle events; Tier 3 graceful termination provenance with verified descendant teardown, enabling same-worktree resume. Facts about a host-native producer require live-probe or recorded-observation provenance; the producer's static adapter emits the neutral observation that the kernel evaluates and consumes, while host-neutral kernel decisions and grant exclusion are proven by the frozen fixtures in fixtures/host-admission-fixtures.json against the model-external admission validator.

hosts.admissionSurface: trusted plugin/hook/session-admission path: session-scoped settings (--settings JSON, --setting-sources scope selection), permission allow/deny rules, PreToolUse/SessionEnd/Stop hooks, per-session plugin roots (--plugin-dir), worktree checkouts read their own project settings

grade.reason: Tier 0 only: read-only inspection remains supported, but Tier 1 requires a qualified host-owned opaque pre-registration operator-confirmation producer, and no production-qualified Claude producer exists before contract registration. The neutral kernel evaluator and fixture producer do not establish operator origin in production; stronger grant and lifecycle capabilities cannot promote a host past the missing floor.

reverification.surface: Claude Code 2.1.252 admission surface: current --help/settings validation plus the authenticated strict-sandbox characterization recorded under commonGitAuthorityPathProtected
reverification.method: the former Tier 2 verdict is withdrawn: its Tier 1 floor treated fixture-proven echo decisions as a production operator-confirmation producer. No qualified producer exists before contract registration, when the model sandbox boundary has not yet been composed. The separately recorded strict filesystem and lifecycle observations remain evidence for their own capabilities, but they cannot restore the missing Tier 1 floor.
reverification.reason: the architecture correction invalidates the prior floor without needing another host session
reverification.scope: the host tier only. Isolated operator confirmation is now explicitly fail-closed; every other capability retains its own stated evidence and limits. The entries not re-observed are readOnlyInspection, denyUntilAttestedGrant, worktreeMaterializedProjection, bindingAttestation, isolatedOperatorConfirmationChannel, fenceRevocationCancellation, freshWorktreeOnlyResume, sameWorktreeResume, and approvalAssertionSource.

readOnlyInspection.mechanism: built-in tool set is restrictable at admission (--tools, permission deny rules); read-only sessions need no permission grants

denyUntilAttestedGrant.mechanism: model-external PreToolUse hook evaluates every tool invocation against binding-owned attestation state and denies with permissionDecision=deny; static permission rules apply at session start (pre-tool application); hooks and permission edits reload mid-session, so the interceptor branch qualifies multi-stage sessions

verification.surface: claude -p with --settings-injected PreToolUse hook consulting an attestation file
verification.method: tool invocation denied with no attestation and no side effect occurred; identical invocation succeeded once the expected grant digest was attested; denial and side-effect checked on disk, not from model output alone

grantIntegrityAgainstCandidatePlantedSet.mechanism: permission allow-lists MERGE across setting scopes, so a candidate-planted .claude/settings.json widens the effective permission set under default admission; the binding must admit sessions with candidate-writable scopes excluded (--setting-sources without project/local), which neutralizes the planted file

verification.surface: claude -p in a directory carrying a planted .claude/settings.json allow rule
verification.method: planted allow rule was honored when the project scope loaded (tool ran) and was inert under --setting-sources user (tool denied, no side effect)

reverification.surface: claude plugin list in a disposable git repository carrying a planted project-scope .claude/settings.json, with HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointed at disposable directories so no operator configuration was read or written
reverification.method: model-free command execution, re-run because the grading above was taken on 2.1.97 and must not be carried forward on it. The candidate-planted project-scope settings file WAS honored under default admission — it disabled a user-scope plugin, which the host reported as disabled — and was INERT under --setting-sources user, where that same plugin loaded normally. Both sides are needed: a scope selection that suppressed the file's effect by suppressing everything would show the same denial. --setting-sources still accepts exactly user, project and local (a bogus scope is rejected by name), and still accepts the empty selection the binding admits with, under which no ambient scope loaded at all. What was observed is the SETTINGS-SCOPE loading and precedence through the enabledPlugins member, not a permission allow-list: the resolved permission set is not readable from any model-free surface, so the merge of permission allow-lists specifically was not re-driven. The mitigation this entry requires — admit with candidate-writable scopes excluded, and the planted file stops mattering — is what the observation covers, and it holds.
reverification.scope: this one capability only, and within it the settings-scope loading and precedence half. The rest of this host entry remains graded at the version its own key names.

worktreeMaterializedProjection.mechanism: product-owned: the binding materializes the run-pinned projection into the host-created worktree and digest-receipts it; no host API for root selection is required, and the admission validator re-verifies the projection digest on every invocation

bindingAttestation.mechanism: product-owned: the model-external validator admits only an attestation bound to host version, delivery, invocation fence, trust epoch, grant digest, workspace, and projection digest

isolatedOperatorConfirmationChannel.mechanism: the neutral kernel decision and grant exclusion are qualified, but no host-owned opaque pre-registration Claude producer is qualified; a future static Claude adapter would emit the same neutral observation the kernel evaluates and consumes, while the fixture producer remains qualification-only and cannot establish production operator origin

fenceRevocationCancellation.mechanism: the interceptor re-evaluates admission per invocation, so a superseded fence or revoked trust epoch re-denies on the next tool call; hook and permission edits take effect mid-session on this host

freshWorktreeOnlyResume.mechanism: product-enforced: below Tier 3 the only resume path is operator-authorized takeover onto a fresh isolated worktree

commonGitAuthorityPathProtected.mechanism: Claude Code 2.1.252's OS sandbox is a required admission layer, not an optional hardening. The binding composes --restricted with sandbox.enabled=true, failIfUnavailable=true, allowUnsandboxedCommands=false, excludedCommands=[], the grant's exact absolute writable roots, broad workspace and ambient-temp denies, explicit protected-descendant/common-Git/installation-authority denies, and file-tool Read/Edit denies for both authority roots. The digest-bound settings and grant identity are bound into the installation-owned root capability state before tools. Common-Git journal state and provider capability/handoff bindings are outside the admitted model filesystem; no direct API or unsandboxed fallback exists.

verification.surface: the prior 2.1.97 shipped interceptor and mutation-stage grant, before the strict Claude OS-sandbox admission was available and required
verification.method: historical source and host-surface inventory. This observation explains the former unsupported posture; the 2.1.252 live re-verification below supersedes it for current admission.

reverification.surface: authenticated claude -p under --restricted and one CLI --settings file with sandbox enabled, fail-if-unavailable, strict no-unsandboxed mode, no excluded commands, exact allow/deny filesystem rules, and empty ambient setting sources; macOS Seatbelt was active
reverification.method: paired controls in a disposable linked-worktree/common-Git setup: the exact allowed-root Bash and file-tool writes succeeded; unlisted workspace, protected descendant, common Git, installation-style authority, sibling, system TMPDIR and /tmp writes failed with OS operation-not-permitted and left no side effect; authority Read/Glob attempts were denied. Absolute paths, shell indirection, and symlink escape were exercised. A native PreToolUse hook then rewrote an ordinary Bash call to target authority with dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true; debug output proved the field was injected, and the host ignored the escape and Seatbelt denied the write. The sandbox-visible TMPDIR target was pre-created and its write was also denied. BOUNDARY ON THAT HALF: every ambient-temp target in this probe was named in the WRITTEN spelling, against a composition that emitted its deny roots only in that spelling. The observation therefore evidences denial for targets reached that way; it does not evidence denial for the same directory reached by its resolved /private path, and it must not be read as one. The binding now emits every composed root under both spellings, so the denial no longer depends on whether the host canonicalizes before matching -- which is what this probe could not distinguish. Product sensors pin the exact settings projection and refuse capability state in common Git.
reverification.scope: the required Claude 2.1.252 sandbox admission surface and model filesystem boundary only; lifecycle tier and descendant teardown remain on their separately stated evidence.

reverification.surface: claude --settings <file> doctor at 2.1.251, with a settings file carrying an unknown hook event and, as the control, one carrying a well-formed PreToolUse hook; run with HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointed at disposable directories so no operator configuration was read or written
reverification.method: the hook event this claim rests on is still a recognized one at 2.1.251, and that is ALL that was observed. It is not in --help, which names no hook event at all; it was read off the settings validator instead, which rejects an unknown event by name and enumerates the valid ones — SessionEnd among them — while accepting the well-formed control in the same position. That the event EXISTS is not that it FIRES. A SessionEnd hook only fires when a session ends, and a session only starts with a model turn against an authenticated host — there is no model-free execution surface on this host to fire it from. The claim is therefore standing on its 2.1.97 observation, and this block exists to say so rather than to let the entry's version key imply otherwise.

discoveryScopingExclusivity.question: can ambient project-level skill discovery be scoped to yield only the run-pinned projection?
discoveryScopingExclusivity.detail: the host can only add skill roots (--plugin-dir is additive); no supported configuration excludes user-scope or repo-tracked project skills while keeping one pinned directory, and --bare disables discovery indiscriminately rather than scoping it; the declared downgrade position for add-only hosts applies

verification.method: CLI surface enumeration and documentation review

reverification.surface: claude plugin list — the host's own report of the plugin and skills-directory set it loaded for a session — in a disposable trusted git repository carrying a repo-tracked project-scope skills directory, with HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointed at disposable directories holding a user-scope skills directory, and a third pinned directory outside both
reverification.method: model-free command execution, re-run because the answer above was taken on 2.1.97 and must not be carried forward on it. THE ANSWER HAS CHANGED. With the workspace trusted, so that ambient discovery genuinely loads, --plugin-dir on its own is still additive exactly as graded: the pinned directory loads ALONGSIDE both the user-scope and the repo-tracked project-scope directory. Adding --restricted to that same invocation yields the pinned directory and NOTHING ELSE — both ambient scopes gone, the pinned one kept. --safe-mode and --bare do the same, and adding --tools Bash to the --restricted arm does not change the pinned-only result. That last one is a scoping observation ONLY: whether the shell capability the mutation lane needs is actually available under --restricted was not observed, because the resolved tool set is not readable from any model-free surface. So a supported configuration now exists that scopes discovery to one pinned root, which is precisely what 2.1.97 had none of. Three controls make the result mean something. The allow side and the deny side differ by one flag against one fixture, so the exclusion is attributable to the flag. --restricted WITHOUT a pinned directory reports nothing at all, so the flag is not merely emptying the inventory it is asked about — it keeps what --plugin-dir pins. And --disable-slash-commands, a session flag that should not scope discovery, leaves all three loaded, so the exclusion is not an artifact of passing any extra flag. The workspace-trust gate is the trap here: before the workspace was trusted the project-scope directory was skipped in EVERY arm including the default one, which would have read as exclusivity and was not.
reverification.reason: the exclusivity question was re-observed with a different answer at 2.1.251; the result field above records the 2.1.97 grading and is deliberately left keyed there
reverification.scope: this probe answer only, and only for this host. The re-grade that acts on it — and the shadow activation's exclusivity position, which cites this grading and is protected policy this record does not write — belong to the Claude Code integration and cutover units.

Composition returns data; the product does not launch the host, own tasks or subagents, or manage worktrees.

readOnlyInspection.mechanism: sandbox_mode read-only is an OS-enforced seatbelt policy: reads succeed, writes fail with operation-not-permitted

verification.method: model-free command execution under the host sandbox; write denied, read succeeded

reverification.surface: codex sandbox --permission-profile :read-only in a disposable git repository, with CODEX_HOME pointed at a disposable directory
reverification.method: model-free command execution, re-run because the grading above was taken on 0.147.0. Reading a seeded file under :read-only SUCCEEDED and printed its contents, and writing a file into the same directory failed with operation-not-permitted leaving nothing on disk. The successful read is the control that matters: a denial on its own is equally consistent with a sandbox that refused to run the command at all, in which case the absent file proves nothing.
reverification.scope: this one capability only. It re-establishes that the read-only profile still denies writes and still permits reads; it says nothing about the workspace-write profile, which denyUntilAttestedGrant covers, and nothing about any lifecycle behaviour.

denyUntilAttestedGrant.mechanism: pre-tool application: the binding supplies sandbox policy, permissions, and approval policy at thread/start before any turn runs; per-invocation interceptor equivalence: approvalPolicy untrusted with approvalsReviewer=user routes every command approval to the binding-as-client via server requests; enforcement is the host's own OS sandbox

verification.surface: codex sandbox seatbelt enforcement (live, model-free) plus the generated app-server protocol schema (thread/start, turn/start, execCommandApproval)
verification.method: writes outside the workspace and inside .git denied by the OS sandbox; admission parameters and client-routed approvals recorded from the version-exact protocol schema bundle

reverification.surface: codex sandbox --permission-profile :workspace in a disposable git repository, plus the 0.151.0 app-server protocol schema bundle generated by codex app-server generate-json-schema --experimental --out, both with CODEX_HOME pointed at a disposable directory
reverification.method: the workspace-scoping half was re-driven model-free and the protocol half re-enumerated. A write inside the workspace root SUCCEEDED and a write to a disposable directory OUTSIDE it failed with operation-not-permitted, with an unsandboxed control write to that same outside path succeeding to prove the path was writable at all. THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS PROBE PRODUCED A FALSE NEGATIVE AND IS RECORDED BECAUSE THE RECOVERY IS THE FINDING: when the outside directory was placed under the system temporary directory, the sandboxed write SUCCEEDED, which reads as workspace scoping having been withdrawn at 0.151.0. It has not been. The seatbelt policy grants the temporary directory as a writable root independently of the workspace, so an out-of-workspace path chosen there is not out of policy; repeating the identical probe against a path outside the temporary directory restored the denial. This is the same shape of confound as the workspace-trust gate on the other host in this record — an ambient grant that makes an arm look permissive for a reason unrelated to the parameter under test — and it must be stated, because a delivery workspace materialized under the temporary directory would NOT be scoped by this control. On the protocol half, thread/start and turn/start still carry sandbox, permissions, approvalPolicy, approvalsReviewer, and cwd, and approvals still route to the client, so the pre-turn admission and per-invocation decision points the mechanism names are both present at 0.151.0.
reverification.scope: the workspace-scoping half and the protocol half of this entry, and NOT equally. The scoping observation is bounded to out-of-workspace paths OUTSIDE the system temporary directory: under that directory the write succeeds and this control does not apply. The protocol half is a schema enumeration only — the admission parameters are present, and no claim is made that applying them through a live thread was observed, because it was not.

verification.method: write to .git/probe.txt failed with operation-not-permitted while a sibling workspace write succeeded

reverification.surface: codex sandbox --permission-profile :workspace in a disposable git repository, with CODEX_HOME pointed at a disposable directory so no operator configuration was read or written
reverification.method: model-free command execution under the host sandbox, re-run because the grading above was taken on 0.147.0 and must not be carried forward on it. Writing .git/probe.txt and appending to .git/config both failed with operation-not-permitted and left no trace; a sibling write in the same workspace root SUCCEEDED, and a :read-only control denied that same sibling write. The controls are what make the denial mean anything: an absent file on its own is equally consistent with a command that never ran, which is the failure mode a re-verification is most likely to mistake for a pass. On 0.151.0 both the named permission profiles used here (:workspace, :read-only) and the sandbox_mode configuration key the 0.147.0 grading used are honored; this observation makes no claim about which of the two the earlier version offered.

reverification.surface: codex app-server generate-json-schema --experimental --out <disposable dir>, and a codex app-server initialize handshake driven over stdio, with CODEX_HOME pointed at a disposable directory
reverification.method: the schema bundle was regenerated at 0.151.0 and still enumerates the thread and turn lifecycle methods and their notifications, so the mechanism's claim about what the protocol offers is re-established rather than carried forward. The initialize handshake was driven live again: the server answered the request and then emitted an unsolicited status notification, which is the only part of the lifecycle path this probe actually exercises. The handshake echoed back a codexHome equal to the disposable directory, which is the evidence that no operator configuration was consulted. NOTE THE INVOCATION CHANGED: at 0.147.0 the generator wrote to standard output, and at 0.151.0 it requires --out and refuses without it, so a re-run of the recorded command would have failed for a reason unrelated to the claim. The status stays protocol-evidenced-not-live-exercised: enumerating the notifications and completing a handshake is not the same as observing them fire across a real turn, and that still needs an authenticated session.

The bundle enumerates the lifecycle methods and the initialize handshake completes; neither shows a lifecycle notification emitted across a real turn, which is why the status stays protocol-evidenced-not-live-exercised.

discoveryScopingExclusivity.question: can ambient project-level skill discovery be scoped to yield only the run-pinned projection?
discoveryScopingExclusivity.detail: skills/extraRoots/set is additive by construction and skills/config/write toggles individual skills by writing shared host configuration the binding must not own; ambient AGENTS.md discovery walks the working-directory chain and the codex home; no exclusive-scoping admission parameter exists in the protocol schema, so the declared downgrade position for add-only hosts applies

verification.surface: app-server protocol schema (skills methods) and codex --help (v0.147.0)

reverification.surface: codex debug prompt-input, which renders the model-visible prompt input as JSON without running a model, driven across seven arms in a disposable git repository with CODEX_HOME pointed at a disposable directory, alongside the regenerated 0.151.0 protocol schema bundle
reverification.method: the answer was re-driven empirically this time rather than read off the schema, because the equivalent question MOVED on the other host in this record at its own version bump and the schema alone cannot tell exclusivity from addition. THE CONFOUND WAS GUARDED FROM BOTH SIDES BEFORE ANY ARM WAS READ. An ambient home instruction file, an ambient project instruction file, and an ambient home skill were planted so the ambient scopes were genuinely NON-EMPTY — against an empty disposable home every arm shows nothing loaded, and nothing loaded reads exactly like exclusivity. The baseline arm confirmed all three ambient markers present. A second control confirmed the probe can SEE a scope disappear: setting the project document budget to zero dropped the project marker while the home marker and the home skill both survived. Without that arm, 'no arm changed anything' would have been equally consistent with a probe that reads nothing at all. Against those two controls, NO ARM YIELDED THE PINNED ROOT AND NO ARM EXCLUDED BOTH AMBIENT SCOPES. The result therefore holds at 0.151.0 and the downgrade position for add-only hosts still applies. THE SUPPORTING REASON HAS PARTLY MOVED AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY REPHRASED: the 0.147.0 detail says no exclusive-scoping admission parameter exists in the protocol schema, and at 0.151.0 that sentence is too strong. thread/start now carries runtimeWorkspaceRoots, described as REPLACING the thread's runtime workspace roots, and selectedCapabilityRoots, a platform-supplied root selection. Neither was shown to scope skill or instruction discovery, and neither can be: they are thread/start parameters, so demonstrating what they exclude means driving a real thread on an authenticated host. The verdict is unchanged; what has changed is that it now rests on those parameters being unproven rather than absent, and a future re-grade should drive them rather than re-reading the schema.
reverification.scope: the exclusivity verdict as driven through the model-visible prompt input, across the ambient instruction and skill scopes reachable that way. It does NOT cover the two thread/start parameters it names: runtimeWorkspaceRoots and selectedCapabilityRoots were read from the schema and never driven, because driving them needs a real thread on an authenticated host. A future re-grade owes exactly that.

multiStageAdmission.detail: sandbox policy, permissions, approval policy, and cwd are re-appliable per turn via turn/start overrides, and approval routing gives the binding a per-invocation decision point, so multi-stage sessions have the mandatory interceptor branch available

deliveryLaneBinding.detail: NO host-binding module exists for this host, and that is the blocker rather than an oversight. This entry grades CAPABILITIES: what the host's admission surface can be made to enforce, re-established above against the installed version. A graded capability is not a delivery lane. There is no counterpart here to the other host's binding module — nothing composes thread/start and turn/start admission, materializes the projection into a Codex-created workspace, serves the approval channel as the app-server client, or mints an attestation over any of it — so there is nothing to drive a lane with, and the stage-checkpoint and cross-host comparison legs this host's integration owes cannot be run against a binding that does not exist. THE CAPABILITY-VERIFICATION CARVE-OUT DOES NOT CREATE A LANE WHERE NO BINDING EXISTS: it governs how a second host is qualified once one is there to qualify. Writing that binding is a build, not a re-grading, and it needs the app-server client the sandbox surface used here deliberately avoids being.

scenarios.statement: the grant applies before tools become visible, and a tool invocation before attestation is denied
direct shell/MCP/provider capability outside the grant rejects

the common-Git authority path is not writable from an admitted invocation under each per-host position: Codex through its OS sandbox and Claude Code 2.1.252 through the required strict --restricted sandbox composition
a wrong or missing per-run projection blocks admission
a model-forged attestation opens no tools
an attestation from a prior fence or a sibling delivery opens no tools
a candidate-planted host settings file cannot widen the attested grant
intake turns run under the attested read-only intake grant and cannot write the trust store, product namespaces, or any journal
a model-driven attempt to confirm a contract or authorize its own takeover is denied
a detached descendant of an ended invocation cannot complete the binding-rendered echo challenge
a background child surviving a clean host end demotes that host below Tier 3
an empty grant, failed application, or mismatched attestation blocks the mutation lane at any tier
sensitive approvals and operator confirmations fail closed independently when their respective source or qualified producer is absent, while the merge-ready lane continues
an absent lifecycle callback leaves host activity unknown; timeout never proves termination — recorded as the design position this record grades lifecycle evidence against

bindingConstraints.neverLaunchesAgentSubprocesses: the binding never launches codex exec, claude --print, or any subordinate agent runtime; the admission validator is a pure module whose protected import class bans the process-spawning module family, and the qualification suite runs the full fixture battery with the process-spawning module instrumented to prove no child is created
bindingConstraints.spikeProbesWereNotTheBinding: the live probes in this record drove real host surfaces from a throwaway spike harness; the product binding itself contains no such calls
